findings.title: Index is built without CONCURRENTLY, which blocks writes on a hot table
findings.explanation: A plain CREATE INDEX takes a SHARE lock on `events` for the whole build. That blocks every INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE on the table. An activity/events table is usually append-heavy and large, so this would stall event writes in production for the duration of the build. Use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`. CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block, so check that the migration tool does not wrap each migration in a transaction. If it does, disable that for this migration (for example a no-transaction directive or flag). Keep this migration to the single statement. Also be aware that a failed concurrent build leaves an INVALID index behind, which must be dropped before retrying.

findings.title: Not idempotent, and a failed concurrent build leaves an invalid index
findings.explanation: Use `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS` so a re-run after a partial failure or manual hotfix does not error out. Note that IF NOT EXISTS will skip an INVALID leftover index, so the runbook should say to check for and drop invalid indexes (`pg_index.indisvalid = false`) before re-running.

findings.title: No evidence the index matches the query or fixes the slow path
findings.explanation: The PR does not include the actual query or an EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) before and after. The index only helps if the query filters on `project_id` and orders by `id DESC`, or paginates by `id < ?`. If it also filters on other columns such as event type or created_at, or orders by a different column, the planner may not use it. Please attach the query and the plan, and confirm the index is chosen on production-sized data.

findings.title: Possible redundancy with an existing index on project_id
findings.explanation: If `events` already has an index on `(project_id)` alone, the new composite index makes it redundant. It would only add write overhead and storage. Check the existing indexes, and if the old one is superseded, drop it in a follow-up migration, also with CONCURRENTLY.

findings.title: Index name and rollback
findings.explanation: The name `events_project_id_idx` does not show the sort order or the second column, so a name like `events_project_id_id_desc_idx` would be clearer. If the project uses down migrations, add one with `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS events_project_id_idx;`. Also mention the expected build time and index size in the PR description for the deploy plan.

```diff
+CREATE INDEX events_project_id_idx ON events (project_id, id DESC);
```
